findings.finding: The plan's Scope lists only the new `code-review-concurrency.md` file, but the overlay will never execute unless it is also wired into the code-review gate: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` enumerates every overlay explicitly in both the `round_a` and `round_b` `batch.criteria:` lists (e.g. `- { prompt: code-review-security, when: "${{ steps.triggers.outputs.include_security }}" }`), fed by the `triggers`/`union` overlay_union steps that emit per-overlay `include_*` outputs. A new overlay with no gate entry (and no `include_concurrency` trigger) is authored-but-unreachable.

findings.finding: The plan will not produce a functioning overlay: a code-review Pass-1 overlay is wired in THREE coordinated places, but Scope/AC deliver only the .md file. It is never added to OVERLAY_IDS (registry.py), gets no criteria_routing.json entry, and gets no dispatch line in code-review.yaml — so the gate never invokes it and it cannot 'own correctness races' as claimed.
scenarios: Gate runs on a diff introducing an unlocked-twin accessor; the concurrency overlay never fires because no glob/content/escalation path selects it and no dispatch step exists.
AC 'pytest tests/unit -k reviewer passes' is satisfied by a lone .md file precisely because nothing wires it in — masking that the overlay is inert.
